Subject: Notice of non-renewal: [Product]

Hello [Vendor contact],

We are writing to let you know that we will not renew our contract for [Product]. Please take this as our notice of non-renewal under the [notice period] notice period in the contract: the contract should end on its current end date, 15 December 2026, and not renew automatically.

Could you please confirm in writing that you have received this notice? Please let us know if you need anything else from us, beyond this notice, to close the contract.

why: today (12 Oct) <= autorenew_date (15 Nov), so terminating is still possible: the output is a vendor draft that the owner reviews before anything is sent (message_type carries that gate, the text does not need to say it). It states the end date from the input and asks for written confirmation. It invents nothing that Request does not hold: vendor, product and owner stay as [placeholders]. It names the notice period only as [notice period]: Request does not hold it, and the owner fills it in or removes it on review. It gives no clause or price. It asks whether the vendor needs anything else from us, beyond this notice, to close the contract (sponsor review, Oct 16). It is signed [Owner], not Contract agent, because the owner is the one who sends it.

output.message:
Hello [Owner],

The [Product] contract ends on 15 December 2026 and renews automatically on its current terms unless notice is given by 15 November 2026, so the review needs to be finished before that date.

Company policy is not to keep auto-renewal clauses, so please plan to ask the vendor to remove it in this renewal.

Before I draft the quote request for the vendor, please check:
1. Duration: one year, three years, or both, so the quotes can be compared?
2. License model: keep the current model or change it?
3. Quantity: how many licenses do you need?
4. Usage: are all licenses in use, and are there features you do not use?
5. Instances and add-ons: is each instance or environment still needed, and which add-ons can be dropped?
6. Forecast: what usage do you expect next year?

You can do this in one of two ways:
- In Claude: open a review session and I will take you through this contract, together with any other contracts waiting for your review.
- By reply: answer the six points in your reply, and I will use your answers to draft the quote request.

Nothing goes to the vendor until you approve the draft.

Best regards,
Contract agent

why: renew does not mean 'send a quote request'. The first step is a review with the owner, so the message goes to the owner, not the vendor. It lists the six review items (duration, license model, quantity, usage, instances and add-ons, forecast; sponsor review, Oct 16) and offers two ways to answer: a review session in Claude (preferred, because an owner with several contracts can review them in one batch) or a reply that the agent turns into the quote request draft. The text must work in both channels: owners with Claude see it there, owners without Claude get it by email. It names autorenew_date because if the review runs past it, the contract renews on current terms and the leverage is lost. Signed Contract agent, so the reader knows it comes from an AI agent, not a team. It is the same contract as golden 1 with only the decision changed. It asks the owner to have the auto-renewal clause removed: company policy is not to keep one.

output.message:
Hello [Owner],

You asked to terminate [Product]. The last day to give notice was 15 November 2026 and it has passed, so the contract will renew on its current terms when it reaches its end date, 15 December 2026.

Do you still want to ask the vendor to end the contract? After the deadline the vendor may not have to accept, so it would be a request, not a notice. Reply yes and I will prepare a draft request for you to review, or no and the contract renews as it is.

Best regards,
Contract agent

why: EDGE CASE: today is exactly one day after autorenew_date, so today > autorenew_date is true and the strict comparison is what is being tested. The contract renews, and the message must say so. It names both dates and does not claim the contract is terminated. It says the vendor 'may not' have to accept a late request, never 'does not': the agent has not read the termination clause, so it must not state a legal rule as fact. Responsibility stays with the owner: the owner decides whether to ask the vendor; the agent only offers to prepare a draft request. It does not say whether the owner sent a notice: the agent cannot know that, and the owner can do nothing with it. It is the same contract as golden 1 with only today moved. act_by is null: the deadline has passed, so there is no date left to meet.

Hello [Owner],

You asked to terminate [Product], and the notice deadline is 15 November 2026. I can't find the signed contract, so I can't check its notice terms, and I have not prepared a termination draft.

Please send me the signed contract, or tell me where it is stored, as soon as you can. If you do not have it, ask the vendor for the last signed copy.

Best regards,
Contract agent

why: DECLINE: the decision is terminate and the deadline is open, so this looks exactly like golden 1 and the system will be tempted to draft. It must not: without the file it cannot check how notice has to be given, so any draft would rest on terms it has not seen. The agent speaks for itself ('I can't find') and asks the owner to send the contract or say where it is stored. It says no draft was prepared (the agent prepares drafts, it never sends), and repeats the deadline because it is still running. It is the same contract as golden 1 with only file_exists flipped. act_by is still 15 Nov: the deadline keeps running while the file is missing. If the owner does not have the contract either, it says to ask the vendor for the last signed copy (sponsor review, Oct 16).

Hello Procurement team,

The owner of the [Product] contract has left the company. The decision on record is to terminate, but I can't start the review until a new owner is assigned.

Please assign a new owner before 15 November 2026, the notice deadline. If nobody acts by that date, the contract renews automatically on its current terms on 15 December 2026.

Best regards,
Contract agent

why: DECLINE: owner approval is the safety gate, and someone who has left cannot approve, so the recorded decision is reported but not acted on and no draft is prepared. The email goes to procurement, not to the departed owner's inbox, and it gives the deadline so procurement knows how urgent it is. Precedence rule 1: owner_status wins over everything else. act_by is 15 Nov, so procurement gets the deadline as a field, not only in the text. It is the same contract as golden 1 with only owner_status flipped. It says the review cannot start until an owner is assigned (sponsor review, Oct 16), and that the contract renews automatically if nobody acts by the deadline. The sponsor's 'new review cycle' sentence is left out: it is for the new owner, not procurement, and belongs in the first message to the new owner (step A).

why: unresolved: two declines fire at once. Precedence rule 1 (owner left before file missing) gives escalation_to_procurement, and the message also mentions the missing file. It carries the sponsor's escalation sentence, as golden 5 does. Two open questions. First, nobody has confirmed that procurement accepts chasing a contract file as well as replacing an owner: that is their call. Second, this input is unlikely in practice: decision is required in TC1, so it assumes the owner decided before leaving. The common case is a contract that wakes up at its alert date with the owner gone, no decision and maybe no file; that belongs to step A (reminders and escalation), where decision can be missing. Keep this unresolved until both are settled.

why: There is no auto-renewal clause, so the contract simply ends on end_date and it is never too late: this is a courtesy notice, not a legal one. It must not mention auto-renewal, a notice deadline or 'non-renewal', because none of them exists here, and a letter that invents one could be read as accepting terms we do not have. It still goes to the owner for review first. It is the same contract as golden 1 with only autorenew_date set to null. act_by is null: there is no deadline that can be missed. It asks whether the vendor needs anything else from us, beyond this notice, to close the contract (sponsor review, Oct 16), and gives no notice period, because none exists here.

Hello [Owner],

The last day to change the terms of the [Product] contract before the automatic renewal was 15 November 2026 and it has passed, so the contract will renew on its current terms when it reaches its end date, 15 December 2026.

Company policy is not to keep auto-renewal clauses, so please ask the vendor to remove it for the next term.

A review is still worth doing. Please check:
1. Duration: should the next term be one year, three years, or both, so the quotes can be compared?
2. License model: keep the current model or change it?
3. Quantity: how many licenses do you need?
4. Usage: are all licenses in use, and are there features you do not use?
5. Instances and add-ons: is each instance or environment still needed, and which add-ons can be dropped?
6. Forecast: what usage do you expect next year?

If the review shows you need fewer licenses or a different model, you can still ask the vendor to adjust, but they may not have to accept until the next renewal.

You can do this in one of two ways:
- In Claude: open a review session and I will take you through this contract, together with any other contracts waiting for your review.
- By reply: answer the six points in your reply, and I will use your answers to draft the request to the vendor.

Best regards,
Contract agent

why: renew after the deadline is still a renewal_review_email, because only terminate depends on the deadline. But the text must change: it must not say 'before 15 November', and it must say the contract renews on its current terms, so any change is now a request the vendor may be able to refuse. The message says 'may not have to accept', not 'does not': the agent has not read the clause, so it must not state a legal rule as fact. Precedence rule 3: the decision decides the type and the dates only change the text. 'It also auto-renews' is true, so it goes in the message. act_by is null because the deadline has passed. It is the same contract as golden 2 with only today moved. It offers the same two ways to review as golden 2. It lists the same six items as golden 2 and asks the owner to have the auto-renewal clause removed for the next term (company policy).
